hook_text: Gold beads for the king, clay pots for the farmers. What can a grave tell us about class?
clip_script: Mokopane, cardboard and foil. The learners press foil over a cardboard rhino, just as the gold smiths of Mapungubwe pressed gold foil over carved wood. Mapungubwe was the first town in southern Africa: thousands of people, many kinds of work, and three levels of society. The royal family on the hilltop, important people near the hill, ordinary people in the valley. Gold objects, like the rhino, the bowl and the sceptre, were buried only with the most important people. Gold meant royal power.
visual_style: Whiteboard triangle in three layers beside a cardboard rhino being wrapped in shining foil.
mood: Hands-on and thoughtful, like a craft lesson with a big idea inside.
pacing: Quick craft opening, steady explanation of the three classes, ending on the golden objects.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the three levels of society at Mapungubwe.
